claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS, and multi-cloud with CDK is nearly impossible.
AWS CDK allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python, while Pulumi supports any programming language.
CDK and CloudFormation generate an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because CloudFormation is slower than direct execution.
AWS CDK supports only AWS Secrets Manager for secrets, while Pulumi supports cross-cloud secrets.
CDK state management uses a CloudFormation state file while Pulumi uses Pulumi-managed state.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation; once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: "With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle."
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS is described in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the Pulumi engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
Through 2023 SST was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion; Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's 'Moving away from CDK' post says that when you run `sst deploy`, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine that calls the bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for providers and deployment engine and Terraform providers are bridged through Pulumi.
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka on dev.to wrote: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'

SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls and @pulumiverse/vercel as direct dependencies, in the anomalyco/sst repository (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package has roughly 796,000 downloads per week (796,291 for Sept 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST itself.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components exist as Pulumi offerings for cross-team visibility, guardrails, and sharing patterns.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
A blog post exists at /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/ telling SST's move off CDK.
